Apollonius of Rhodes, The Argonautica, translated by Arthur S. Way.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/apollonius-of-rhodes/the-argonautica/arthur-s-way

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Apollonius of Rhodes, the author, died about 215 BC (Wikidata Q192638, P570 = -0215-00-00).
- Arthur S. Way, the annotator and the translator, died 1930 (Wikidata Q4800630, P570 = 1930-09-25).

First publication of the text used: 1901 (SE colophon: 'The Argonautica was completed in the early third century BC by Apollonius of Rhodes. It was translated from ancient Greek in 1901 by Arthur S. Way.')

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1901, before 1931, so it is in the United States public domain.
- Country of origin: the facts do not name the country of first publication. The possible countries are the United Kingdom, Ireland, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India and South Africa. Each of these has a term of life + 70 years or less. The United States is also possible, and the text was first published before 1931, so the United States rule settles that case (see above). The last person named above, Arthur S. Way, died in 1930, so the text entered the public domain in each of the other possible countries on 1 January 2001.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
